name: Saturn V
dispatch: The Saturn V existed to solve one brutal piece of arithmetic: putting a crew on the Moon means throwing roughly 45 tonnes onto a path out of Earth's gravity, and in 1961 nothing on Earth could throw a fraction of that. So von Braun's Marshall team built the largest machine that had ever flown — five F-1 engines at its base, each the most powerful single-chamber rocket engine ever fired at the time, together burning some thirteen tonnes of propellant every second. Everything about it was sized by the destination, not by what looked reasonable. That it flew thirteen times and never once failed to reach space is the part that still doesn't quite seem possible.
description: The 110.6 m three-stage rocket that put 24 humans on a translunar trajectory and 12 of them on the lunar surface. Thirteen launches between 1967 and 1973, zero losses on ascent. The most powerful rocket to reach orbit for over five decades until Starship's Super Heavy surpassed it in 2024.
